headline: An active, stormy week is ahead for western Washington: on-and-off showers today, then a series of stronger storms Tuesday through Thursday bringing widespread rain, gusty winds, mountain snow, high surf and a growing threat of coastal flooding, including higher tides along the Strait of Juan de Fuca and Puget Sound shorelines later in the week.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: A low-pressure system parked off the Washington coast keeps sending showers onshore all day Sunday, so Sequim, Port Angeles and the Puget Sound lowlands can expect on-and-off showers, with some of the interior rain evaporating before it reaches the ground and the heaviest showers along the coast, where a few could turn briefly stormy this afternoon. Highs run in the mid to upper 40s for most interior spots; around Seattle, clouds may dip lower (40% chance) through about 1 PM as the morning showers wrap up, before more showers return this evening. Snow levels drop to about 2,000–3,000 feet late tonight, and a Winter Weather Advisory runs from 6 PM Sunday to 4 PM Monday for the Olympics, where Hurricane Ridge could see 5 to 10 inches of snow.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Monday brings a wave of steadier precipitation, mostly focused on the Olympics and Cascades, with showers over the interior lowlands and snow levels rising to about 4,000 feet by afternoon; winds come down the Cascades with gusts near 23 mph Monday morning. Another front arrives Tuesday, and a stronger one moves over western Washington Tuesday into Wednesday as the offshore low deepens, bringing widespread lowland rain, mountain snow with Cascade snow levels around 3,000–3,500 feet, and locally breezy winds, strongest along the coast.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: More strong storms follow Wednesday into Thursday with another round of widespread rain, breezy winds and mountain snow. Rain looks heaviest Wednesday night into Thursday, especially over the Olympics; no widespread river flooding is expected, but the Skokomish River will likely reach minor flood stage around midweek and stay there through the weekend, and a Hydrologic Outlook has been issued. Winds turn more southerly to southwesterly on Thanksgiving Day, and the discussion says little about Friday and Saturday on land beyond a brief lull in the wind Friday morning.

coast: A Coastal Flood Advisory runs from 7 AM to 3 PM Sunday for the Grays Harbor County and northern Washington coasts. High tides plus the coming storms raise the coastal flood threat, especially along the Pacific coast during Tuesday's high surf, and confidence is growing that moderate to major flooding could occur along parts of the Grays Harbor County coast with Wednesday's tides, made worse by high surf. Tides rise more significantly along the Strait of Juan de Fuca and Puget Sound shorelines (including the Sequim and Port Angeles shore) from Tuesday onward, and impacts there will be watched closely. On the water, southeast winds of 23–35 mph (20–30 knots) continue over the coastal waters and the east Strait, with a Small Craft Advisory until 4 PM Sunday for the east entrance of the Strait and until 10 PM Sunday for the coastal waters, a new advisory for the Grays Harbor Bar as seas build to 9–12 feet, and a slight chance of thunderstorms over the coastal waters this afternoon and evening. A Gale Watch covers the Strait of Juan de Fuca and the coastal waters from Sunday evening through late Tuesday night: late Sunday into Monday brings southeast winds of 23–35 mph with gusts to about 40 mph, and Monday evening through late Tuesday looks worst, with widespread gale-force gusts and a better than 60% chance of storm-force gusts (about 55 mph or more) over the outer coastal waters. Another round of strong gales comes Wednesday into Thursday (50% chance of storm-force gusts), with interior waters seeing more wind on Thanksgiving as winds turn south-southwest; after a brief break Friday morning it stays breezy offshore into the weekend. Seas build to 18–22 feet Tuesday, ease to 16–20 feet Wednesday and Thursday, and drop to 10–12 feet Friday into the weekend.
watch_for: Coastal flooding: moderate to major flooding possible on the Grays Harbor County coast with Wednesday's high tides, and rising tides along the Strait of Juan de Fuca and Puget Sound shorelines from Tuesday onward.
Skokomish River likely in minor flood from midweek through the weekend.
Timing and strength of the Monday-night–Tuesday and Wednesday–Thursday storms (gales on the water, heavy Olympic rain).
confidence: Forecasters are confident in showers today and an active, stormy pattern through the week, with growing confidence in coastal flooding along the Grays Harbor County coast Wednesday, but the exact impacts along the Strait and Puget Sound shorelines are still uncertain and will be watched closely.
